hook.line: Someone you respect invites you somewhere you cannot go, and a flat *no puedo* feels too cold. Spanish has a few polite phrases that say no and show you mean it.
hook.es: Me temo que no voy a poder.
hook.en: I'm afraid I won't be able to.

examples.es: Me temo que no voy a poder.
examples.en: I'm afraid I won't be able to.

examples.es: Me temo que no va a ser posible.
examples.en: I'm afraid that won't be possible.

examples.es: Sintiéndolo mucho, no puedo ir al concierto: tengo turno en el café.
examples.en: Much as I regret it, I can't go to the concert: I'm on shift at the café.

examples.es: Sintiéndolo mucho, me resulta imposible acompañarte ese día.
examples.en: Much as I regret it, it's impossible for me to go with you that day.

examples.es: Me temo que Vale no va a poder venir hoy.
examples.en: I'm afraid Vale won't be able to come today.

examples.es: Me resulta imposible aceptar la oferta de Altamira.
examples.en: It's impossible for me to accept Altamira's offer.

rule:
Three polite ways to refuse:

*Me temo que* + a normal verb: "I'm afraid that…". *Me temo que no voy a poder.*
*Sintiéndolo mucho,* + what you cannot do. It means "much as I regret it".
*Me resulta imposible* + infinitive: "it's impossible for me to…".

*Me temo* is not real fear. It is a cushion before bad news. *Sintiéndolo mucho* is a little formal, like a letter.

Give the reason after the refusal (*tengo turno en el café*). A bare no still sounds cold, even with the polite frame.
smallPrint: Teachers call *sintiéndolo mucho* a gerund used as a concessive phrase.

readAndPick.es: Sintiéndolo mucho, no puedo ir al concierto: tengo turno en el café.
options: Much as I regret it, I can't go to the concert: I'm on shift at the café.
I'm so glad I can go to the concert: I'm on shift at the café.
They regret that I can't go to the concert: I'm on shift at the café.

readAndPick.es: Me temo que no voy a poder.
options: I'm afraid you won't be able to.
I'm afraid I will be able to.
I'm afraid I won't be able to.

readAndPick.es: Me temo que no va a ser posible.
options: I'm sure that will be possible.
I'm afraid that won't be possible.
I'm afraid I'm not going.

readAndPick.es: Me temo que Vale no va a poder venir hoy.
options: I'm afraid Vale won't be able to come today.
Vale is afraid she won't come today.
I'm afraid I can't come today, Vale.

readAndPick.es: Me resulta imposible aceptar la oferta de Altamira.
options: Altamira finds it impossible to accept my offer.
I accepted the impossible offer from Altamira.
It's impossible for me to accept Altamira's offer.

readAndPick.es: Sintiéndolo mucho, me resulta imposible acompañarte ese día.
options: Much as I regret it, it's impossible for me to go with him that day.
Much as I regret it, it's impossible for me to go with you that day.
Much as I regret it, it was impossible for me to go with you that day.

readAndPick.es: Me temo que ya no queda tinto.
options: I'm afraid you don't want coffee.
I'd love for some coffee to be left.
I'm afraid there's no coffee left.

readAndPick.es: Me temo que no vamos a poder abrir mañana.
options: I'm afraid we won't be able to open tomorrow.
I'm afraid I won't be able to open tomorrow.
I'm afraid they won't be able to open tomorrow.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *Me temo* or *Sintiéndolo mucho*, then type the whole sentence: ___ que no voy a poder.
yourTurn.answer: Me temo que no voy a poder.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm afraid that won't be possible.
yourTurn.answer: Me temo que no va a ser posible.
yourTurn.why: *Me temo que* opens, then a regular future with *ir a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm afraid Vale won't be able to come today.
yourTurn.answer: Me temo que Vale no va a poder venir hoy.
yourTurn.why: The *no* sits before *va a poder*, as in any sentence.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Much as I regret it, I can't go to the concert: I'm on shift at the café.
yourTurn.answer: Sintiéndolo mucho, no puedo ir al concierto: tengo turno en el café.
yourTurn.why: The reason after the colon makes the refusal feel real.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It's impossible for me to accept Altamira's offer.
yourTurn.answer: Me resulta imposible aceptar la oferta de Altamira.
yourTurn.why: *Me resulta imposible* is followed by an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: *Me temo que no voy a poder.* becomes: I'm afraid we won't be able to.
yourTurn.answer: Me temo que no vamos a poder.
yourTurn.why: *Me temo* stays; only the verb after *que* changes to *vamos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish, to a friend: Much as I regret it, it's impossible for me to go with you that day.
yourTurn.answer: Sintiéndolo mucho, me resulta imposible acompañarte ese día.
yourTurn.why: *Acompañarte* has *te* attached, because the friend is *tú*.

pitfalls.wrong: Tengo miedo que no voy a poder.
pitfalls.right: Me temo que no voy a poder.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Tengo miedo* is real fear; *me temo que* is the polite "I'm afraid".

pitfalls.wrong: Sintiendo mucho, me resulta imposible acompañarte.
pitfalls.right: Sintiéndolo mucho, me resulta imposible acompañarte.
pitfalls.why: You need the little *lo* ("it") on the end, and the accent that goes with it.

pitfalls.right: Sintiéndolo mucho, no puedo ir: tengo turno en el café.
pitfalls.why: A bare no still sounds cold, so add the real reason.

personal: Think of an invitation you would turn down. Refuse it with *Me temo que no…* or *Sintiéndolo mucho,…* and give a reason.
